Common causes: the Spring Data JPA dependency is missing or not on the Eclipse classpath, project dependencies haven’t been refreshed, or there’s a conflicting build configuration.

Fix (brief):
- Ensure you have Spring Data JPA on the classpath (add to `pom.xml` or `build.gradle`).
- Refresh project dependencies in Eclipse (Maven > Update Project or Gradle > Refresh).
- Verify import is `org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository`.
- If you use `module-info.java`, export/require modules or remove the module file for now.

Example dependency snippets.

Maven (`pom.xml`):
```xml
<!-- Add this inside <dependencies> -->
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-jpa</artifactId>
</dependency>
```

Gradle (`build.gradle`):
```groovy
dependencies {
  implementation 'org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-data-jpa'
}
```

Eclipse refresh:
- Right-click project -> Maven -> Update Project... (check "Force Update of Snapshots/Releases")  
-or-  
- Right-click project -> Gradle -> Refresh Gradle Project.

If it still fails, show `pom.xml` or `build.gradle` and the exact IDE error message.

reply.text:
Likely cause: adding `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa` without a JDBC driver or datasource configuration causes Spring Boot to fail auto-configure a DataSource (common error: "Cannot determine embedded database driver class for database type NONE" / "Failed to configure a DataSource"). Also verify your `pom.xml` uses a Spring Boot parent/BOM and that `MealRepository` imports `org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository`.

Quick fixes:
- Add an embedded DB dependency for local dev (H2) or your DB driver (e.g., MySQL).
- Ensure `pom.xml` uses `spring-boot-starter-parent` (or Spring Boot BOM).
- Refresh Maven in Eclipse (Right-click project → Maven → Update Project).
- Add minimal datasource properties in `application.properties`.

Example `pom.xml` (add/merge into `pom.xml`):
```xml
<!-- xml -->
<parent>
  <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
  <version>3.1.5</version> <!-- use the version you need -->
  <relativePath/> 
</parent>

<dependencies>
  <dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-jpa</artifactId>
  </dependency>

  <!-- H2 for local development -->
  <dependency>
    <groupId>com.h2database</groupId>
    <artifactId>h2</artifactId>
    <scope>runtime</scope>
  </dependency>

  <!-- optional web starter -->
  <dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
  </dependency>
</dependencies>
```

Example `application.properties` (add to `src/main/resources`):
```properties
# properties
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb
spring.datasource.driverClassName=org.h2.Driver
spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.password=
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
spring.h2.console.enabled=true
```

Also verify your repository interface uses the correct import:
```java
import org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository;
```

If the error persists, open `pom.xml` and the exact runtime error message.

Short diagnosis and checklist:
- Most common causes: missing JDBC driver on the classpath, missing/incorrect `spring.datasource.*` properties, or network/credentials problems to the DB.
- In Eclipse: right‑click project → Maven → Update Project… (force update), then restart the app.
- Check the exact startup log error (e.g., "Cannot determine embedded database driver class for database type NONE" or "Failed to configure DataSource") and share it if it persists.

Quick fixes — add a runtime DB driver and minimal properties.

Description: add an embedded H2 for quick local testing (or your DB driver like MySQL/Postgres) and set datasource properties in `src/main/resources/application.properties`.

```xml
<!-- pom.xml: add a runtime DB dependency (H2 example) and ensure spring-boot-starter-data-jpa is present -->
<dependencies>
  <dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-jpa</artifactId>
  </dependency>

  <!-- H2 for local/dev -->
  <dependency>
    <groupId>com.h2database</groupId>
    <artifactId>h2</artifactId>
    <scope>runtime</scope>
  </dependency>

  <!-- Example: MySQL driver (use only if connecting to MySQL) -->
  <!--
  <dependency>
    <groupId>mysql</groupId>
    <artifactId>mysql-connector-java</artifactId>
    <scope>runtime</scope>
  </dependency>
  -->
</dependencies>
```

```properties
# src/main/resources/application.properties
# H2 in-memory (quick local setup)
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb
spring.datasource.driverClassName=org.h2.Driver
spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.password=
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
spring.h2.console.enabled=true

# --- OR: example MySQL settings (uncomment and edit for a real DB) ---
# spring.datasource.url=jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/yourdb?useSSL=false&serverTimezone=UTC
# spring.datasource.username=youruser
# spring.datasource.password=yourpassword
# spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
# spring.datasource.driver-class-name=com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver
```

Extra checks:
- Ensure `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa` is in `pom.xml`.
- Confirm the DB driver jar is on the classpath (Maven dependency present and downloaded).
- Verify network/credentials when using a remote DB.
- If you see a MapStruct/bean error earlier, ensure `MealMapper` is a Spring bean (e.g., `@Component` or `@Mapper(componentModel="spring")`) and returns real mappings — but that won't let the app start if the DataSource fails.

If it still fails, paste the exact startup error log and your `pom.xml` and `application.properties`.
